title: Egy szép vázát: Adjective + Object in the Past

sections.title: Only the noun takes the ending
sections.content: Describing what you bought, saw, or found often means putting an adjective in front of the object — and only the NOUN takes the case ending; the adjective in front stays in its plain dictionary form. Vettem egy szép vázát. ("I bought a beautiful vase") — szép never becomes *szépet, only váza becomes vázát. This holds for definite objects too: Megvettem a szép vázát. ("I bought the beautiful vase").

items.english: I bought an expensive gift for Ildikó.

items.spanish: Megvettem a drága ajándékot, amit a boltban láttál.
items.english: I bought the expensive gift you saw in the store.

items.spanish: Láttam egy régi ismerőst a piacon.
items.english: I saw an old acquaintance at the market.

sections.content: This is exactly the rule you already use with present tense (Olvasok egy érdekes könyvet.) — nothing changes when you move the whole sentence into the past.
